src/MoveBG/MapObjHide.cpp called the MSL intrinsic __fabsf directly where the public fabsf wrapper exists; the intrinsic only moves the score.
Use the wrapper unless the binary proves the intrinsic call; a direct intrinsic call is flagged for review (sms_intrinsic_bypass), not rejected outright.
Apply the accepted SMS upstream rule; validate the retained source against binary and map evidence.
Do not commit dummy arrays, locals, fabricated storage or other tricks to force a stack frame match, with or without volatile and regardless of the name.
When the frame is the only remaining difference the function is done: leave it nonmatching, with no comment.

src/Enemy/bosseel.cpp:1570 declared a Mtx44 and a TVec3 that the function never reads or writes, purely to grow the frame.
Unreferenced locals of any type are dummy storage; remove them and leave the frame nonmatching, with no comment.
A file-scope placeholder class in a .cpp hides the real owner and blocks other units from using the type.
Look up __vt__/__dt__/__ct__ in config/GMSJ01/symbols.txt: symbols in another unit mean the class belongs there; symbols in this unit mean move it to this unit's header, with no marker comment.
src/Camera/lensglow.cpp TLensGlow ctor wrapped the path buffer in a union with a u64 only to force 8-byte alignment and the frame size ("super ultra fakematch", doldecomp/sms #331).
Alignment tricks are banned outright; the real cause is likely a missing inline. Keep the plain buffer and leave the frame nonmatching.
M3DUtil/MActor: seven `x >= 0` tests were rewritten as `0 <= x`. Building both ways showed each flip added exactly 8 bytes of frame and changed no instruction (doldecomp/sms #330).
An operand swap is normal matching only when it changes non-stack codegen; check with toolpacks/gamecube-decomp/_impl/gamecube/tools/stack_check.py hunks and revert stack-only swaps.
PAD_STACK is the Melee padding form; SMS bans it and anything like it.
Humans find the real inlines; AI matching stops at the frame and leaves the function nonmatching, with no comment.
In SMS a helper invented to explain the stack shape is a fabricated inline, marked or not.
Use the real inline when a header, the map or a sibling decomp shows it; otherwise call the function directly and leave the frame nonmatching.
A `this` alias and a literal local used once usually only shape registers and the stack.
In SMS keep such a local only when building both ways (toolpacks/gamecube-decomp/_impl/gamecube/tools/stack_check.py hunks) shows a non-stack codegen change; stack layout is not a reason.
